jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
The Challenged Athletes Foundation® (CAF) is a world leader in helping individuals with physical disabilities get involved and stay involved in sports and fitness. CAF believes that participation in sports at any level increases self-esteem, encourages independence, and enhances quality of life. Since 1994, CAF has provided millions of dollars in grants and resources that empower individuals with physical disabilities to pursue active lifestyles through sport. CAF is headquartered in San Diego, California, with additional regional presence across the United States.

Position overview:

The Chief Operating Officer role is a new role to the organization. CAF is looking for a COO to help lead the organization through its next phase of growth and impact. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Director, the COO will serve as a key strategic partner, ensuring alignment between vision, operations, people and performance across the organization. This role requires an experienced leader that can maintain and build upon the culture of the organization while simultaneously guiding the organization through the change management necessary to secure the future of the organization. 

Who we're looking for: 

The right person for this role is highly strategic, financially sophisticated, and they thrive at the intersection of leadership, accountability, and execution. This individual will play a critical role in strengthening organizational performance while helping build a culture where leaders think and operating like true owners of their departments. 

The ideal candidate: 

Possesses exceptional financial acumen and a deep understanding of budgeting, forecasting, resource allocation, performance metrics and financial stewardship.
Has a proven track record of driving organization-wide financial accountability and helping leadership teams make decisions grounded in data, outcomes, and fiscal responsibilities.
Can successfully facilitate a strategic shift in leadership focus toward operational excellence, measurable results, and sustainable financial performance.
Provides support to leaders that allows them to take ownership of their functions, empower department heads to think strategically, manage resources effectively, and operate with an enterprise-wide mindset.
Brings outstanding communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to serve as a trusted bridge between the Board of Directors, executive leadership, and operational teams.
Is comfortable engaging with board members on strategy, organizational performance, financial health, and key business initiatives while translating board priorities into actionable organizational outcomes.
Balances strategic vision with hands-on, execution oriented leadership style.
Is passionate about mission driven work and creating meaningful impact in the community.

Responsibilities: 

Organizational Leadership and Execution: 

In partnership with the Chief Executive Director, this role will translate organizational strategy into actionable operational plans, priorities and performance objectives.
This role will directly support the Chief Accounting Officer, Chief Marketing Officer, Chief Programs Officer and the HR function.
They will assist in establishing department goals that are aligned to the organization priorities.
The COO will remove roadblocks, assist to establish and operationalize plans, and align departmental projects so the team is able to make an impact.

Financial and Operational Stewardship:

In partnership with the Chief Accounting Officer, this role will be engaged in the development, implementation and monitoring of annual budgets.
Maintain accountability for organizational resource allocation, ensuring investments align with strategic priorities and operational requirements.
Monitor department financial performance and recommend corrective actions when performance deviates from budget or plan.
Identify and implement cost effective solutions that improve organizational efficiency while maintaining service quality and mission impact.

Process improvement, Data and Reporting:

Lead organizational process improvement initiatives including workflow redesign, standardization and continuous improvement efforts. Drive technology
Oversee organizational reporting systems and create performance dashboards to ensure timely, accurate and actionable information is available to leadership.
Establish and monitor KPI's and organizational metrics that measure operational, programmatic and financial performance.
Utilize operational and financial data to support strategic planning, decision making, and organizational sustainability.
Drive technology adoption and process integration initiatives

Total Rewards Strategy at CAF: 

CAF offers a competitive compensation package, commensurate with experience. The expected salary range for this position is between $150,000 - $170,000. CAF also offers a complete benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401k match, generous vacation and holiday schedule, hybrid work schedule, onsite weekly team lunches, an engaging culture, and a dog friendly work place. 

Qualifications: 

Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree in Business Administration, Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, or related field preferred. 
Minimum of 7-10 years of progressive nonprofit leadership experience.
Demonstrated experience leading operational functions within a nonprofit organization.
Strong financial acumen, including budget development, financial analysis, forecasting, and resource management.
Experience overseeing multiple departments and leading cross-functional teams.
Proven ability to develop strategic plans and translate them into measurable operational outcomes.
Experience utilizing data, reporting, and performance metrics to drive organizational improvement.
Excellent leadership, communication, interpersonal, and relationship-building skills.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
Demonstrated success managing change and improving organizational processes.
Ability to work effectively with executive leadership, board members, staff, volunteers, donors, and community stakeholders.
Commitment to CAF's mission and values.
Willingness to travel and work occasional evenings and weekends as required

Director of Development

About Monsignor Scanlan High School

Monsignor Scanlan High School is a Catholic, college-preparatory school in the Bronx dedicated to educating young men and women in an environment rooted in faith, academic excellence, leadership, and service. Guided by the values of the Gospel, Scanlan prepares students to become compassionate leaders committed to serving their communities and living lives of purpose.

We are seeking a visionary, relationship-driven Director of Development to lead the school's advancement program and build a sustainable culture of philanthropy that strengthens Scanlan's future.

Position Summary

Reporting directly to the Chairman the Board of Trustees and the Board of Trustees, the Director of Development serves as the school's chief advancement officer and is responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive fundraising strategy that advances the school's long-term priorities. The Director leads all aspects of philanthropy, including major gifts, annual giving, planned giving, grants, donor stewardship, and campaign strategy while cultivating meaningful relationships with alumni, parents, foundations, corporations, and community leaders.

The Director provides leadership and supervision for the Development Office, managing Development and Alumni staff to ensure the effective execution of fundraising operations, alumni engagement, communications, and special events.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a strategic fundraiser who enjoys building relationships, inspiring philanthropy, managing a high-performing team, and helping shape the future of Catholic education.

Key Responsibilities

Advancement Leadership

Develop and implement a comprehensive fundraising strategy aligned with the school's priorities.

Lead annual giving, major gifts, planned giving, grants, and capital fundraising initiatives.

Establish fundraising goals, monitor progress, and evaluate results.

Supervise and mentor advancement staff and manage the Development Office budget.

Donor & Board Relations

Build and manage a portfolio of major gift prospects.

Cultivate, solicit, and steward donors, foundations, and corporate partners.

Serve as staff liaison to the Board of Trustees and Development Committee.

Partner with the Principal and Board to advance fundraising priorities and support trustees in donor engagement.

Advancement Operations

Oversee donor stewardship, database management, fundraising reporting, and grant proposals.

Provide strategic oversight of alumni engagement and fundraising events, delegating day-to-day planning to staff.

Collaborate with school leadership to advance institutional priorities.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree.

Five or more years of fundraising or advancement experience with demonstrated success in major gifts.

Experience supervising staff.

Excellent communication, organizational, and relationship-building skills.

Preferred

Experience with donor databases (Blackbaud Raiser's Edge preferred).

Experience in Catholic education, independent schools, or higher education.

Grant writing and campaign experience.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate is a strategic leader who is passionate about Catholic education, inspires philanthropy, builds lasting relationships, develops high-performing teams, and serves as an effective ambassador for Monsignor Scanlan High School.

Compensation & Benefits

Salary: Starting at $75,000 to $100,000, commensurate with experience.

Comprehensive benefits include medical, dental, vision, retirement, paid time off, and professional development opportunities.

Application Instructions

To apply, please submit resume and cover letter to brivera@scanlanhs.edu, subject Director of Development Application. No calls or recruiters, please.

Send applications or inquiries to: brivera@scanlanhs.edu

About The Employer

Monsignor Scanlan High School is a Catholic co-educational secondary school, dedicated to the vision of its founder, Rev. Msgr. Arthur J. Scanlan, which celebrates traditional Christian values, and the diversity of society; provides an education which emphasizes high academic standards, social awareness, and spiritual development; creates a family atmosphere that challenges, yet nurtures; cultivates an appreciation for the worth and dignity of every individual; fosters dedication to community service; and develops a life-long commitment to the realization of maximum personal potential.

Company Description:

The Boys & Girls Club of Paterson & Passaic is a youth development organization dedicated to inspiring and enabling young people, especially those who need us most, to reach their full potential as productive, responsible, and caring citizens. The Club provides a safe, supportive after-school environment for children and teens ages 5 to 18, as well as a summer day camp. Professional staff and volunteers deliver a wide range of high-quality educational, social, and recreational programs at an accessible annual membership fee, ensuring broad community participation. Programs focus on core areas such as character and leadership development, education and career readiness, and health and life skills, equipping young people with the tools to build positive relationships, pursue future goals, and maintain healthy lifestyles.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Program Director supervises and manages the planning, organizing, and conducting of programs, activities, and events, providing individual guidance as needed in the Clubhouse. The Program Director implements and supports engaging and age-appropriate programs within the priority outcome areas of Academic Success, Healthy Lifestyles, Good Character, and Citizenship, and demonstrates to staff how to incorporate youth development principles; provide guidance to club members and their families; and manages behaviors resulting in a safe and positive environment for youth. Under the direction of the Executive Director of the Department of Youth Employment and Opportunity, the Deputy Director is responsible for leading the department to be an organization that maximizes its external impact while focusing on internal effectiveness and efficiency. The Deputy Director will serve as a critical member of the YEO Leadership team, and alongside the Department Executive Director will manage strategy and execution across all program teams & services. This role will also lead efforts to implement new initiatives for the department.

The position is designed for an individual who embodies a genuine passion for the department's mission of employing, developing, and engaging Boston youth by amplifying youth voices and bridging opportunities for personal and professional growth.

Strategic Management and Leadership:

Oversees the department's general personnel and staff teams (including interns and indirect reports) and provides day-to-day leadership to support productivity, performance, and development of all.

Employment (youth recruitment, onboarding, and payroll processes)

Career-readiness (curriculum development and workshop administration)

jobs.description:
CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER: VIKR TECHNOLOGIES, INC.

THE SHORT VERSION

VIKR Technologies, Inc. is hiring its first Chief Executive Officer. The company was incorporated in Delaware on 22 September 2026. The technology is built and working, the patent application is filed, and there is no CEO, no outside capital, and no customers yet. That is the job.

Compensation is $5,000 per month while you raise, capped at six months, then $150,000 to $185,000 once the round closes, and 5% of the company.

The founder holds VIKR's stock through a holding company and stays out of operations by design and by written federal ethics approval. The CEO runs it, reporting to the board. That is not a disclaimer; it is the structure.

If you have closed a seed round before and know the investors who fund government technology, keep reading. If you have not, this is not the seat.

THE PROBLEM

Proving that a government contractor is who it claims to be still runs on phone calls, screenshots, and paperwork that is out of date the moment it prints. A prime carries real exposure for its subcontractors' standing, and the only tools are manual lookups, repeated by a compliance team for each contract and each contractor.

There is no fast way to verify where a contractor actually stands, at the source. So everyone downstream is trusting stale information and hoping it holds.

WHAT VIKR DOES

VIKR issues a digital credential that carries its own proof.

A contractor's standing is gathered from multiple independent authoritative sources, not a single government list, and cross-checked against each other, so no one record can be wrong or gamed. The verified result is sealed into a credential with a signature that cannot be faked or altered, carrying a record of where each piece came from.

Anyone checking confirms in seconds that it is genuine, sees what it is based on, and makes their own call. No login, no portal, no phone call, and it works offline, because audits happen in rooms without connectivity.

Verify once at the source, trust it everywhere after. VIKR supplies the proof; the party checking keeps the decision.

We know of no one holding this position today. Registries verify and data vendors aggregate, both on platforms the checker must log into. Nobody issues a portable standing credential for federal contractors that the contractor holds and anyone can verify without calling the issuer.

WHERE THINGS STAND TODAY

Incorporated in Delaware on 22 September 2026.

A patent family is with outside patent counsel. An omnibus provisional application was filed on 18 September 2026, securing priority.

The production system runs end to end today, from source data to a signed credential that anyone can verify. It is documented well enough to hand to the technical hire on day one.

What does not exist yet: a CEO, a technical co-founder, outside capital, and paying customers. In that order.

THE MANDATE

Days 1 to 30. Hire the founding Chief Technology Officer. You get the full technical briefing on day one under NDA. That hire's terms are already set: 12% equity with a monthly stipend until salary triggers on a revenue or financing milestone, so you recruit against a defined offer.

Months 1 to 5. Build and run the investor pipeline and close the seed round: $2,000,000 minimum on a standard post-money SAFE at a $6,000,000 post-money cap. This is the first job, not a secondary duty.

Months 3 to 6. Product development with the Chief Technology Officer, toward first customer demonstrations.

Months 6 to 12. First paying customers, the first 50 to 100 credentialed organizations, and the start of the Series A narrative.

Months 12 onward. Series A preparation begins. The round is projected for the first half of 2029 at roughly $1,500,000 in annual recurring revenue: $8,000,000 to $12,000,000 at $25,000,000 to $35,000,000 pre-money.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN A YEAR

The round is closed, the technical co-founder is shipping, the first customers are paying, and the company depends on the founder for nothing but the intellectual property it licenses.

WHO THIS IS FOR

You have closed a seed or SAFE round. Not attempted. Closed.

You can name the partners at funds that back government, defense, or compliance technology, and reach them this month. Cold outreach takes six to nine months; warm relationships take six to nine weeks. That difference is the job.

You have operated inside or next to federal contracting, procurement, compliance, or defense technology, and can hold your own with investors who know the market.

You can see why the first market is an entry point rather than a ceiling, and can say so without overpromising.

You have six to twelve months of personal financial runway. The consulting fee is capped at six months, and salary starts only when the round closes. That is structural, not a negotiating position.

You have the network to hire a founding Chief Technology Officer within thirty days of your own start.

You are authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.

You are comfortable with a founder-owner who built the technology and the intellectual property, engages at board level, and stays out of daily operations.

WHO THIS IS NOT FOR

Anyone who needs a salary from day one. Anyone who wants to be handed a funded company. Anyone who treats fundraising as someone else's job. Anyone who needs the founder to make decisions for them.

COMPENSATION

Before the round closes: a $5,000 per month consulting engagement funded by the founder's holding company. It is a consulting fee, not deferred salary, capped at six months or $30,000, whichever comes first. If the round has not closed by then, the arrangement ends. That is why the mandate targets a close inside five months, and why personal runway matters.

At close: base salary of $150,000 to $185,000.

Equity: 5% of the company on a fully diluted basis. 1% granted when you start, 4% unlocking at the close, both vesting over four years from your start date with a one-year cliff, subject to a 409A valuation, with an 83(b) election required within 30 days of each grant. The cliff is deemed satisfied if the round closes before your first anniversary, after which vesting continues monthly on the same schedule.

The 5% is measured before the seed round. The round and the employee option pool dilute it, as they dilute everyone, including the founder.

Performance bonuses: up to $30,000 in the first year after close and up to $80,000 in the second, tied to named milestones.

Title: Chief Executive Officer. Strong commercial candidates one step below a sitting chief executive may start as President with a board-confirmed path to CEO. Same mandate either way.

Location: the Washington, DC area or Texas preferred. Remote considered for exceptional candidates.

Restrictive covenants are standard and negotiated in the employment agreement.

HOW THE COMPANY IS STRUCTURED, AND WHY IT MATTERS TO YOU

The founder holds VIKR's stock through Frami Hald, LLC, which also owns the intellectual property and licenses it to VIKR under an agreement that executes before the seed round. The founder is not an officer, director, employee, or signer, and is not in the operational reporting chain. This is under a written federal ethics opinion and an approved outside-activity request, and it holds for as long as the federal employment does.

For a chief executive that means real authority: you run the company and report to the board, not to the founder. It also means clean governance, the first thing an investor checks when the intellectual property sits in a related entity.

An independent director holds the board seat and makes the hiring decision for this role. The Chief Executive Officer reports to the board. The board is small by design and grows as the company raises.

WHAT YOU GET ON DAY ONE

A working product, a filed patent application, complete technical documentation, an executed intellectual property assignment, a Delaware corporation with clean governance, and an independent director who has already done the formation work. The license from the holding company is drafted and executes before the seed round.

PROCESS

Write to info@vikrtechnologies.com with three things: the round you closed and its size, the investors you can reach in this market, and your runway before a close.

If there is a fit, we sign a mutual non-disclosure agreement, and you get the full briefing package: business plan, investor materials, technical detail.

Conversations with the founder follow, then with the independent director, who makes the appointment and the offer.

QUESTIONS PEOPLE ASK

Why isn't the founder running it? The founder is a federal employee. The structure was cleared in writing before the company was formed, and it is why the CEO seat carries genuine authority.

Is the technology real, or a deck? It runs, and you will see it running once the NDA is signed.

Who owns the intellectual property? The founder's holding company owns it and will license it exclusively to VIKR under an agreement executed before the seed round. At the Series A, VIKR holds an option to buy it outright at a price set by an independent valuation. The arrangement is disclosed to every investor in advance.

Why hasn't it raised yet? The raise is the CEO's first mandate. The founder cannot lead it.

What if the round does not close in six months? The consulting arrangement ends. Whether the seat continues past that is the board's decision.

What happens to the founder's role later? It does not change during federal employment: owner and board-level participant through the holding company, nothing more.

APPLY

info@vikrtechnologies.com. A mutual non-disclosure agreement is required before full briefing materials are shared.

VIKR Technologies, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer.

CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER: VIKR TECHNOLOGIES, INC.

THE SHORT VERSION

VIKR Technologies, Inc. is hiring its first Chief Executive Officer. The company was incorporated in Delaware on 22 September 2026. The technology is built and working, the patent application is filed, and there is no CEO, no outside capital, and no customers yet. That is the job.

Compensation is $5,000 per month while you raise, capped at six months, then $150,000 to $185,000 once the round closes, and 5% of the company.

The founder holds VIKR's stock through a holding company and stays out of operations by design and by written federal ethics approval. The CEO runs it, reporting to the board. That is not a disclaimer; it is the structure.

If you have closed a seed round before and know the investors who fund government technology, keep reading. If you have not, this is not the seat.

THE PROBLEM

Proving that a government contractor is who it claims to be still runs on phone calls, screenshots, and paperwork that is out of date the moment it prints. A prime carries real exposure for its subcontractors' standing, and the only tools are manual lookups, repeated by a compliance team for each contract and each contractor.

There is no fast way to verify where a contractor actually stands, at the source. So everyone downstream is trusting stale information and hoping it holds.

WHAT VIKR DOES

VIKR issues a digital credential that carries its own proof.

A contractor's standing is gathered from multiple independent authoritative sources, not a single government list, and cross-checked against each other, so no one record can be wrong or gamed. The verified result is sealed into a credential with a signature that cannot be faked or altered, carrying a record of where each piece came from.

Anyone checking confirms in seconds that it is genuine, sees what it is based on, and makes their own call. No login, no portal, no phone call, and it works offline, because audits happen in rooms without connectivity.

Verify once at the source, trust it everywhere after. VIKR supplies the proof; the party checking keeps the decision.

We know of no one holding this position today. Registries verify and data vendors aggregate, both on platforms the checker must log into. Nobody issues a portable standing credential for federal contractors that the contractor holds and anyone can verify without calling the issuer.

WHERE THINGS STAND TODAY

Incorporated in Delaware on 22 September 2026.

A patent family is with outside patent counsel. An omnibus provisional application was filed on 18 September 2026, securing priority.

The production system runs end to end today, from source data to a signed credential that anyone can verify. It is documented well enough to hand to the technical hire on day one.

What does not exist yet: a CEO, a technical co-founder, outside capital, and paying customers. In that order.

THE MANDATE

Days 1 to 30. Hire the founding Chief Technology Officer. You get the full technical briefing on day one under NDA. That hire's terms are already set: 12% equity with a monthly stipend until salary triggers on a revenue or financing milestone, so you recruit against a defined offer.

Months 1 to 5. Build and run the investor pipeline and close the seed round: $2,000,000 minimum on a standard post-money SAFE at a $6,000,000 post-money cap. This is the first job, not a secondary duty.

Months 3 to 6. Product development with the Chief Technology Officer, toward first customer demonstrations.

Months 6 to 12. First paying customers, the first 50 to 100 credentialed organizations, and the start of the Series A narrative.

Months 12 onward. Series A preparation begins. The round is projected for the first half of 2029 at roughly $1,500,000 in annual recurring revenue: $8,000,000 to $12,000,000 at $25,000,000 to $35,000,000 pre-money.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN A YEAR

The round is closed, the technical co-founder is shipping, the first customers are paying, and the company depends on the founder for nothing but the intellectual property it licenses.

WHO THIS IS FOR

You have closed a seed or SAFE round. Not attempted. Closed.

You can name the partners at funds that back government, defense, or compliance technology, and reach them this month. Cold outreach takes six to nine months; warm relationships take six to nine weeks. That difference is the job.

You have operated inside or next to federal contracting, procurement, compliance, or defense technology, and can hold your own with investors who know the market.

You can see why the first market is an entry point rather than a ceiling, and can say so without overpromising.

You have six to twelve months of personal financial runway. The consulting fee is capped at six months, and salary starts only when the round closes. That is structural, not a negotiating position.

You have the network to hire a founding Chief Technology Officer within thirty days of your own start.

You are authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.

You are comfortable with a founder-owner who built the technology and the intellectual property, engages at board level, and stays out of daily operations.

WHO THIS IS NOT FOR

Anyone who needs a salary from day one. Anyone who wants to be handed a funded company. Anyone who treats fundraising as someone else's job. Anyone who needs the founder to make decisions for them.

COMPENSATION

Before the round closes: a $5,000 per month consulting engagement funded by the founder's holding company. It is a consulting fee, not deferred salary, capped at six months or $30,000, whichever comes first. If the round has not closed by then, the arrangement ends. That is why the mandate targets a close inside five months, and why personal runway matters.

At close: base salary of $150,000 to $185,000.

Equity: 5% of the company on a fully diluted basis. 1% granted when you start, 4% unlocking at the close, both vesting over four years from your start date with a one-year cliff, subject to a 409A valuation, with an 83(b) election required within 30 days of each grant. The cliff is deemed satisfied if the round closes before your first anniversary, after which vesting continues monthly on the same schedule.

The 5% is measured before the seed round. The round and the employee option pool dilute it, as they dilute everyone, including the founder.

Performance bonuses: up to $30,000 in the first year after close and up to $80,000 in the second, tied to named milestones.

Title: Chief Executive Officer. Strong commercial candidates one step below a sitting chief executive may start as President with a board-confirmed path to CEO. Same mandate either way.

Location: the Washington, DC area or Texas preferred. Remote considered for exceptional candidates.

Restrictive covenants are standard and negotiated in the employment agreement.

HOW THE COMPANY IS STRUCTURED, AND WHY IT MATTERS TO YOU

The founder holds VIKR's stock through Frami Hald, LLC, which also owns the intellectual property and licenses it to VIKR under an agreement that executes before the seed round. The founder is not an officer, director, employee, or signer, and is not in the operational reporting chain. This is under a written federal ethics opinion and an approved outside-activity request, and it holds for as long as the federal employment does.

For a chief executive that means real authority: you run the company and report to the board, not to the founder. It also means clean governance, the first thing an investor checks when the intellectual property sits in a related entity.

An independent director holds the board seat and makes the hiring decision for this role. The Chief Executive Officer reports to the board. The board is small by design and grows as the company raises.

WHAT YOU GET ON DAY ONE

A working product, a filed patent application, complete technical documentation, an executed intellectual property assignment, a Delaware corporation with clean governance, and an independent director who has already done the formation work. The license from the holding company is drafted and executes before the seed round.

PROCESS

Write to info@vikrtechnologies.com with three things: the round you closed and its size, the investors you can reach in this market, and your runway before a close.

If there is a fit, we sign a mutual non-disclosure agreement, and you get the full briefing package: business plan, investor materials, technical detail.

Conversations with the founder follow, then with the independent director, who makes the appointment and the offer.

QUESTIONS PEOPLE ASK

Why isn't the founder running it? The founder is a federal employee. The structure was cleared in writing before the company was formed, and it is why the CEO seat carries genuine authority.

Is the technology real, or a deck? It runs, and you will see it running once the NDA is signed.

Who owns the intellectual property? The founder's holding company owns it and will license it exclusively to VIKR under an agreement executed before the seed round. At the Series A, VIKR holds an option to buy it outright at a price set by an independent valuation. The arrangement is disclosed to every investor in advance.

Why hasn't it raised yet? The raise is the CEO's first mandate. The founder cannot lead it.

What if the round does not close in six months? The consulting arrangement ends. Whether the seat continues past that is the board's decision.

What happens to the founder's role later? It does not change during federal employment: owner and board-level participant through the holding company, nothing more.

APPLY

Join our team supporting the University of Iowa’s Tippie College of Business and play a pivotal role in advancing our mission. This position involves optimizing a dynamic portfolio of major gift prospects, guiding them through a well-established donor engagement process. Collaboration with fellow UI Center for Advancement fundraisers and leveraging relationships with campus leaders will be key to developing strategic fundraising priorities.  Models the role of a trusted philanthropic advisor, using transparent communication and educating donors about the giving process

Cultivation

 Manages portfolio of active major gift prospects and develops their readiness to advance
 Builds travel plans demonstrating judicious use of time and resources, including strategic meetings with active prospects and additional qualification and stewardship meetings
 Develops and implements donor-centric cultivation strategies, collaborating with colleagues as needed
 Manages deliberate sequence of interactions with each prospect, intended to build engagement and move them through the steps of an established donor engagement process
 Maintains expert knowledge of funding priorities within and beyond assigned unit, consulting with UICA colleagues and campus partners as needed
 Facilitates prospects’ decision-making process; helps them understand next steps and articulate the link between their personal objectives and institutional priorities
 Maintains expert knowledge needed to ensure donors are fully informed about the full range of planned giving options

Negotiation

 Meets expectations for solicitations, gifts closed, and average gift size (goals established annually with the supervisor in alignment with organization-wide metrics)

Reporting directly to the Chief Medical Officer, this senior leadership role will champion the growth, development, and success of APPs across our national network of nephrology practices. Reporting to the Chief Medical Officer, the APP Program Director is a senior advanced practice provider (NP or PA) responsible for leading, connecting, and elevating APPs across all Panoramic Health practice sites. This role serves as the primary APP liaison to physician and operational leadership, standardizes clinical protocols and onboarding, develops education and mentorship programs, and partners with the VP of Provider Growth on recruiting, school partnerships, retention, and platform expansion.

Duties And Responsibilities

Serves as the primary bridge between APPs and physician, clinical, and operational leadership; represents the APP team in leadership forums and ensures two-way communication across the platform.
Chairs the APP Council and leads regional APP representatives through quarterly all-council meetings and monthly regional check-ins to surface local insights, deployment needs, and provider concerns.
Designs and delivers a recurring APP education program, including clinical updates, case reviews, protocol training, CME opportunities, and service-line readiness across all sites.
Leads structured onboarding for incoming APPs and establishes peer mentorship pathways to accelerate confidence, productivity, and integration into PH's clinical model.
Establishes consistent clinical protocols across APP settings, reducing variation and aligning workflows with physician expectations and organizational standards.
Monitors APP clinical quality metrics, identifies best-practice opportunities, and drives continuous improvement in collaboration with clinical and operational leadership.
Provides oversight for APP documentation standards, including incident-to billing requirements, note accuracy, appropriate supervision protocols, and other compliance expectations across practice settings.
Partners with the VP of Provider Growth on APP recruitment, retention, and platform expansion to align provider capacity with growth strategy and reduce time-to-start.
Builds relationships with NP and PA programs to create a sustainable candidate pipeline aligned with PH's specialty care model.
Facilitates cross-site APP meetings, huddles, peer learning forums, and real-time clinical support channels to strengthen community and reduce provider isolation.
Supports rapid regional deployment and cross-site coverage by working through regional APP representatives and peer networks before escalating to broader staffing solutions.
Advocates for APP development, scope-of-practice clarity, workload balance, and career pathways so APPs are seen as valued contributors across the organization.
Performs other duties and responsibilities as required, assigned, or requested.

NP or PA credential with active clinical license required.
Advanced clinical degree or certification required as applicable to licensure.
Ongoing CME and specialty practice education required; nephrology or related specialty care training preferred.

Experience

5+ years of specialty practice experience required.
Experience as a senior NP or PA with demonstrated clinical leadership, education, mentorship, or onboarding responsibilities.
Multi-site, platform, or geographically distributed practice experience preferred.
Experience partnering with recruiting/provider growth teams and NP/PA school programs preferred.
Nephrology or adjacent specialty care experience preferred.
Specialty practice expertise with the ability to translate frontline clinical experience into scalable standards.
Ability to design education, onboarding, CME, case review, and protocol training programs across distributed sites.
Strong partnership skills with physician leadership, operational leadership, and Provider Growth teams.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and comfort using data and reporting to monitor program execution and quality.
